title: ただのカード
subject: a retired man who rides one-car local trains on summer weekdays to small-town city halls to collect the free municipal manhole cards, the only adult in a queue of children on summer holiday at the sewerage counter, until a clerk runs out in her sandals to show him the real painted cover on the crossing outside
caption: Japanese big band swing in the classic medium-tempo dance-band tradition, the sound of Japan's student and pro big bands. A cup-muted trumpet section playing soft, punchy figures that build to full-band brass hits in the last chorus; a warm trombone section with a growling plunger-muted trombone solo; a saxophone section led by alto playing smooth soli lines; a walking upright bass; swing drums on brushes in the verses moving to sticks on the ride cymbal. Warm, roomy, live-in-a-hall mix with the horns placed by section. Male baritone crooner, relaxed and conversational with a smile in the voice, gentle vibrato on held notes. 118 BPM, Bb major. Unhurried, amused and quietly amazed. No electronic drums, no synths, no autotune, no hip-hop beat, no lo-fi crackle.
lyrics:
[Intro - muted trumpets, brushed drums and walking bass]

[Verse 1]
定年して 三年目の夏
時刻表に 赤い丸つけて
一両だけの 各駅停車で
知らない町の 市役所へ

[Pre-Chorus]
二階のすみの 下水道課
夏休みの列に 大人は俺だけ

[Chorus]
一人一枚 ただのカード
表に町の マンホール
麦わら帽子に はさまれて
「お願いします」と 頭を下げる

[Verse 2]
カードの写真は ツツジとお城
色まで塗った 鉄のふた
「本物 見ます?」って 窓口の人
サンダルのまま 外へ駆けだす

[Chorus]
一人一枚 ただのカード
役所の前の 横断歩道
麦わら帽子と しゃがみこんで
「ほんとだ」って 声がそろう

[Bridge - plunger-muted trombone solo, then bass and brushes only]
四十年 電車で 通ったけど
足もとなんて 見なかった

[Chorus - full band, brass hits behind the vocal]
一人一枚 ただのカード
帰りの電車で 並べてみる
九十八枚 どれもみんな
毎日 誰かが 踏んでる絵

[Outro - saxophone soli and a soft final chord]
